summary: Transfer one body from authored or kinematic motion to solver-owned dynamics at one declared instant while preserving pose and a finite linear/angular release velocity.
objective: A moving body released at the handoff frame continues from the same world pose and velocity under dynamics, with no snap, zero-velocity drop, double transform writer or stale animation overwrite.
applies_when: An animation, drag controller or kinematic trajectory releases an object into rigid-body dynamics.
The outgoing motion must contribute linear or angular momentum after the ownership switch.
intent_signals: release an animated object into physics without losing momentum
switch kinematic platform cargo to dynamic
example_prompts: Animate a crate along a conveyor, then release it into Rapier with its current linear and angular velocity.
Let me drag and throw a tool while proving only the physics body owns its pose after release.
negative_signals: Leaving AnimationMixer and the solver writing the same transform after release.
Estimating velocity from one pose or from variable display-frame deltas without a declared sampling rule.
not_for: Inferring physically valid momentum from an arbitrary teleport or discontinuous animation.

principles: Define one handoff instant and one transform owner on each side. At the instant, both representations agree on world pose; immediately after it, only the dynamic body advances that pose.

Preserve finite center-of-mass linear velocity and angular velocity. For a position-based kinematic Rapier body, read its solver-deduced body velocity after the final kinematic step when the binding exposes the required convention; otherwise derive angular velocity and center-of-mass velocity from declared fixed-time world samples. If animation samples the body origin at velocity v_origin while the center of mass has body-local offset r_COM, use v_COM = v_origin + omega cross (R r_COM), with quaternion sign continuity and stated conventions.
A discontinuity, zero/negative sample interval or nonfinite velocity is a failed handoff. Diagnose it instead of silently fabricating momentum.
implementation: Keep the visual mesh under an identity sync node or convert its world pose into the rigid body's world frame. At the boundary, stop or mask the animation/controller, copy world translation and unit quaternion to the body, change it to dynamic, set the captured center-of-mass linear and angular velocities, and wake it.
Order the transaction so no render frame observes two writers: sample outgoing state, disable outgoing authority, initialize/wake dynamics, then begin body-to-mesh synchronization.

Reset disables dynamic ownership, clears forces/velocities and sleep state as needed, restores the authored start pose/time, and re-enables exactly the original writer. Pause freezes the active model clock without performing a second handoff.
observable_checks: Across the handoff, position and orientation are continuous within declared tolerances and the first dynamic velocity matches the captured release velocity.

An off-center center-of-mass fixture translating and spinning about its authored origin continues with the expected center-of-mass velocity, including the omega cross offset term; a deliberately discontinuous authored pose is rejected or released with an explicitly chosen zero-velocity policy.
After release, changing the old animation time does not move the body. Reset and repeat produce the same handoff state and owner sequence.

creative_affordances: Use a conveyor latch, magnetic rail, character throw or mechanical ejector; the look and release cue remain open choices.
A velocity arrow and owner badge may make the transition inspectable without changing the simulation.
known_limits: This contract does not establish correct mass, collision shape, force model or continuous collision detection.
Finite-difference velocity can be noisy and animation easing may not represent a physical trajectory; record the chosen sampling method.
Authored guidance only; no Rapier world, Three.js scene, Blender animation or rendered handoff was run.

claims.statement: In Rapier, dynamic bodies are affected by forces and contacts, while position-based kinematic bodies remain user-positioned and have velocity deduced from their next positions; kinematic bodies do not yield to contact forces.
claims.scope: Rapier JavaScript body-type semantics; application handoff ordering is authored guidance.

source_refs.locator: RigidBodyType.Dynamic and KinematicPositionBased; kinematic contact-force limitation
Velocity relevance by body type and automatically deduced kinematic velocity

claims.statement: Rapier defines rigid-body linear velocity at the center of mass. Its JavaScript 3D RigidBody API exposes a body-type change with a wake-up argument and methods to inspect and set linear and angular velocity; setting velocities with wake-up is documented for dynamic bodies.
claims.scope: Live generated @dimforge/rapier3d API and JavaScript user guide read 2026-09-08; exact installed binding version must be verified.
